acv.quote: A hundred and eighty K a year, on a three-year term.

data.reason: A Fetchwell engineer used our docs and sandbox to build a working sitter pay flow over a weekend. That turned a bake-off into a yes for Daniel. Priya says she 'barely sold this.'

trigger.action: Lead with paying sellers locally when launching in new countries.
trigger.why: Fetchwell was launching Canada, then the UK, and needed to pay sitters locally in each.
trigger.quote: sitters have to get paid locally

decider.action: Aim the main message at the engineering head, not finance.
decider.why: Daniel, VP of Engineering, signed. The CFO joined for ten minutes and asked one question.
decider.quote: this is an engineering decision, finance will sign what I bring them

competitor.action: Answer 'what do we lose' upfront: PayPal, Venmo, saved cards.
competitor.why: After a Braintree call, Fetchwell's questions turned to losses. Priya only guesses what Braintree told them.
competitor.quote: It went from 'how fast can we build this' to 'what do we lose.'

message.action: Drop the acceptance-rate uplift claim for low-value bookings like these.
message.why: Daniel brushed off the average improvement slide because Fetchwell's average booking is 38 dollars.
message.quote: our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates

proof.action: Add a story of a similar-size customer moving saved cards without losing any.
proof.why: Daniel asked for this. Priya never answered, and it came up again at kickoff unresolved.
proof.quote: who's done this at our size without losing cards?

words.action: Say 'stop babysitting' payments, not 'programmable financial infrastructure.'
words.why: Daniel kept saying payments shouldn't need a team. He called their code 'a haunted house.'
